description: Sanity's Content Lake from an agent. Query documents with GROQ, create and edit drafts, publish, upload images and files, read history, run Sanity's AI Agent Actions, manage datasets and webhooks, and receive signed document webhooks.

api.description: Have Sanity's AI write content into a document's fields from an instruction, following the schema. Writes to the draft unless forcePublishedWrite; noWrite returns it without saving. Costs one Sanity AI credit.

fields.description: The deployed schema the action reads, for example _.schemas.default. List them with schemas.list; a project deploys one with 'sanity schema deploy'.
Return the result without saving anything. Not with async.
Start the action and return the target document id at once; the write lands later. For long generations.
Write to the published document instead of its draft, so the change is live at once. Default false.
Needed for the action to write date and datetime fields: { locale: 'en-US', timeZone: 'Europe/Oslo' }.
The dataset to use. Left out: the connection's dataset, else production.
What to write, for example "Write an SEO description of $title under 160 characters".
Values for $names in the instruction: a string, { type: 'constant', value }, { type: 'field', path, documentId? }, { type: 'document', documentId? } or { type: 'groq', query, params? }.
An existing document to write into. Or give targetDocument.

fields.type: { operation: edit | create | createIfNotExists | createOrReplace, _id?: string, _type?: string, initialValues?: Record<string, any> }
fields.description: Where the result goes: { operation: 'create', _type: 'post' } writes a new document, { operation: 'edit', _id } an existing one. Writes go to the draft unless forcePublishedWrite.
Which fields to write, for example { path: 'title' } or [{ path: ['body'] }, { path: 'description', operation: 'set' }]. Left out, every field the action can write.

fields.type: { _id: string, _type?: string, _rev?: string | null, _createdAt?: string | null, _updatedAt?: string | null }
fields.description: The document as the action left it; with async, only its _id, since the write happens later.

api.description: Create a document as a draft (default) or, with publish: true, publish it at once. Returns its id and draft id.

fields.description: The new document's fields: { _type: 'post', title: '...', slug: { _type: 'slug', current: '...' } }. Objects in arrays need a unique _key. Read the dataset's schema or an existing document of the type for its fields.
false (default): the document is created as a draft, which nothing reading published content sees until documents.publish. true: created and published at once.
When a draft with this id already exists: fail (default) errors, ignore leaves it and returns. Only the draft is checked: with an _id of a published document, a new draft is made over it.
Check the change without making it.
The dataset to use. Left out: the connection's dataset, else production.
The transaction that made the change. Missing when there was nothing to change.
The published id. Pass it to documents.publish, documents.edit and the rest.
The draft, drafts.<id>.
Whether the change was also published in this call.

api.description: Throw away a document's unpublished changes (its draft). The published version stays. With purge, the draft also leaves the history.

api.description: Apply raw Sanity mutations (create, createOrReplace, createIfNotExists, patch, delete, by id or by query) in one transaction. For anything documents.create, edit, patch and delete can't express.

fields.description: Sanity mutations, applied in one transaction: { create: {...} }, { createOrReplace: {...} }, { createIfNotExists: {...} }, { patch: { id, set, ... , ifRevisionID } } or { delete: { id } }. A patch or delete can take query + params instead of id to hit every match. They write the exact ids given: a published id is live at once.
Your own id for the transaction. Sending one already used is refused, so a retry cannot apply twice.
Return each changed document. Default false: ids only.
sync (default): answer once queries see the change. async: answer on commit. deferred: fastest, for bulk imports.
Add a _key to array objects that have none.
The dataset to use. Left out: the connection's dataset, else production.

api.description: Run a GROQ query against a dataset and get its result. Reads published documents unless perspective says otherwise. Pass user input as params.

fields.description: A GROQ query, for example *[_type == 'post' && defined(slug.current)] | order(publishedAt desc)[0...10]{ _id, title, 'slug': slug.current }. Project only the fields you need and slice the results: answers above 1 MB can be cut off on Corsair's cloud.
Values for $parameters in the query, without the $: { type: 'post' } for $type. Pass user input this way, never by building it into the query.

Which version of each document the query sees. published (default): live documents only. drafts: drafts where they exist, else published. raw: everything, drafts and release versions under their own ids. A list of release names reads those releases stacked over published, for example ['rSummerLaunch', 'drafts'].
The dataset to use. Left out: the connection's dataset, else production.
The query's result: any JSON value.
Server time in milliseconds.

api.description: Create a webhook that POSTs to a URL when documents matching a GROQ filter are created, updated or deleted. Set a secret so deliveries can be verified.

fields.description: Where Sanity sends deliveries. For a Corsair app, its webhook endpoint (add ?tenantId= when several tenants share one Sanity project).
The dataset to watch, or '*' for all. Left out: the connection's dataset.
Which changes fire it. Unpublishing fires delete.
A GROQ filter, for example _type == 'post'. Left out: every document.
The body to send, as a GROQ projection, for example { _id, title, 'slug': slug.current }. Left out: the whole document.
Fire on drafts too. Default false: published documents only.
Signs every delivery. Store the same value with keys.set_webhook_signature: deliveries without a valid signature are refused.
